title: Educating Businesses on Protection of Customers' Data and Enhancing Punishment Against Hacking
what_it_is: Educating Businesses on Protection of Customers' Data and Enhancing Punishment Against Hacking

sections.label: SMEs in Data Protection Essentials
sections.summary: SMEs may participate in IMDA and PDPC's Data Protection Essentials programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: SMEs may participate in the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) and PDPC's Data Protection Essentials programme (DPE).

sections.label: Penalties for unauthorised personal information offences
sections.summary: Convicted perpetrators face fines up to $5,000 or two years' imprisonment, while knowingly dealing in hacked personal information carries up to $10,000 or three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Perpetrators are liable, upon conviction, for a fine not exceeding $5,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Knowingly obtaining or dealing in personal information that has been obtained through unauthorised access is also punishable under the CMA, with a fine of up to $10,000 or imprisonment of up to three years, or both.

sections.label: Penalties for benefiting from offences
sections.summary: Those who acquire, possess, use, conceal or transfer offence benefits, or help another retain them, face fines up to $500,000 or 10 years' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Persons who knowingly acquire, possess, use, conceal or transfer the benefits of such offences, or assist another to retain such benefits, are liable to a fine not exceeding $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 10 years, or to both.

sections.label: PDPA penalty framework enhancement
sections.summary: The PDPA was amended in 2020, and from 1 October 2022 penalties reach up to 10% of annual turnover in Singapore or $10 million, whichever is higher.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: In fact, the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) was updated and amended in 2020, a couple of years ago, to reflect this growing trend that we see.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: And one important update to the PDPA was the enhancement of the penalty framework, which took effect from 1 October 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: With the amendment and update, which came into effect on 1 October 2022, it is up to 10% of an organisation's annual turnover in Singapore or organisations with annual local turnover exceeding $10 million, whichever is higher.

sections.label: Dealing in hacked personal information
sections.summary: One notable amendment criminalised dealing in hacked personal information, with specifics under the Computer Misuse Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: One of the notable amendments was the criminalised act of dealing in hacked personal information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: On the specifics of the hackers being caught and some of the penalties that have been meted out, I do not have the specific information now because it is under the Computer Misuse Act.
